pais.texto:
South Africa has twelve official languages. English is the first language of under 10% of the population, but it is the language of the news, the law and business.
South African English took words like braai and lekker from Afrikaans. And there, a traffic light is called a “robot”!
fatos: 12, including English, Zulu, Xhosa and Afrikaans

lesson.introText: Today, we’ll talk about South Africa. We’ll take a look at its languages, food, wildlife and history.
lesson.introSub: Twelve languages, braai, wildlife and history

warmup.question: What images come to your mind when you think of South Africa?
Why do you think a country would have twelve official languages?

fotos.texto: A braai is much more than a barbecue: it is the gathering itself. South Africans invite friends with: “Come for a braai!”
Half a loaf of bread, hollowed out and filled with curry. It was invented by the Indian community of Durban.
One of the largest wildlife parks in Africa, with lions, elephants and rhinos.
The prison island where Nelson Mandela spent 18 years. Today it is a museum and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
A stretch of coast in the south of the country, with forest, beaches and lagoons.
The singer who took songs in Xhosa to stages around the world.

lesson.vocabSub: words you will hear in South Africa · pay attention to pronunciation

languageGame.question: South Africa has only one official language.
In South Africa, a traffic light is called a “robot”.
Nelson Mandela spent 18 years on Robben Island.
Bunny chow is a dish made with rabbit meat.
languageGame.explanation: It is half a loaf of bread, filled with curry.

languageGame.question: In Kruger National Park, you can see lions, elephants and rhinos.

conversation.question: English is the first language of under 10% of South Africans, but it runs the news, the law and business. Why do you think that is?
Choosing one big local language could give an advantage to one group. Should a country choose a “neutral” language instead? What are the pros and cons?
Is it fair that English is the language of business in so many countries? Why (not)?
Many South Africans switch languages in the middle of a sentence. Is that a skill or a problem, in your opinion?
South African English took words like braai and lekker from Afrikaans. Which English words have entered Brazilian Portuguese? Is that good or bad?
Ubuntu means “a person is a person through other people”. How does this idea apply to your life?
Robben Island, where Mandela spent 18 years, is a museum today. Why is it important to keep places connected to a difficult past?
Desmond Tutu and Nelson Mandela, two South Africans, won the Nobel Peace Prize. Who do you admire for working for peace or justice?
How can wildlife parks like Kruger balance tourism and the protection of animals?
South Africa has three capitals, one for each branch of government. Is that efficient? Why (not)?
Would you rather go on a safari or drive along the Garden Route? Why?

evaluation.question: Did you enjoy talking about South Africa?
Which other countries would you like to learn more about?
